text_en: You can always find a home in Hafin.
May adventure be with you in Terragaya, if that is what you seek!
Edil
Edil arrived here some years ago, just as you have. She looked so upset, so I took care of her; I welcomed her as if she were my own daughter.
I'm trying to instruct her in the ways of magic, but she is too stubborn. I often catch her fantasising about her chivalrous adventures.
The mission

These Valkyries came up with the same contrived story for everyone but, you know what? We didn't die to be part of any war of the Gods. Your General Brigard seems like a sensible man. I believe he hopes to find the “Guardian” with another goal in mind. Do you really think it'll be able to take you back? To be quite honest with you, I very much doubt this Guardian even exists.
Hafin

This city welcomes anyone in search of peaceful coexistence for the rest of time, although not everyone is able to adapt to a city like this. Many beings prefer to lead another lifestyle in other parts of Terragaya, either because of the weather or because they are unable to coexist peacefully.
Valkyries
You must not fear them. Their only task is to bring us into this world when our time is up, although... for some reason, your time ended somewhat abruptly.
I'm sorry you ended up here; it doesn't seem like it's your time yet. I mean, if you looked 400 years old like Jivan, I'd understand, but...
Edil, I'm right here.
(And even if you weren't, you could hear me even inside the house).

As I was saying, I know it can be a bit sad at first, but you get used to it in the end. Jivan became my family and, even though he's a grouchy old hermit, I've never felt alone ever since he took me in.
You could say that I owe him my life, or my second life, that is...
I can't lie to you. I love it when adventurers like you come to Hafin. Do you know how many times I've imagined myself traveling around Terragaya in armour like that, facing danger?!
Jivan is too protective of me. He doesn't let me set foot outside the city. It'll be hard for me to convince him that I can defend myself.
But I won't bore you with my problems. Stop by every once in a while. I look forward to hearing all about your adventures!
Stop by every once in a while. I look forward to hearing all about your adventures!
Greetings, soldier. Do you have something to discuss?
Make your way to the desert lands of <color=LOC>Sibuna</color>, west of the Spider Lair, in search of <color=CHA>Adamont</color>. Head out as soon as possible.
The mission

For the time being, we shall focus on gathering information. It seems that this entire city has decided to ignore the Valkyries' request and many do not believe that the "Guardian" even exists, but if there's a chance we can make it back to our world, we cannot rule it out yet.
Hostile soldier
I received reports of soldiers suddenly attacking their comrades. Witnesses confirm that the attitude of these soldiers did not seem voluntary. I wonder what is happening to them...
Arkzel
Arkzel's whereabouts are still unknown. I saw him moments before the earthquake. Could he be stuck somewhere?
For my best friend, I'd do anything, at any time.
Wow! One of those Human newcomers.
Come on, if you'd like to know what we can do for you, I'll tell you.
As engineers, Krath and I deal with all kinds of gadgets, so if you have something like a <color=OBJ>Secondary Weapon</color>, we can upgrade it for you.
As long as you bring enough <color=OBJ>Asgarite</color>.
Alright, let's see what we have here.
Wow, man! The soldier bloke again.
Indecisive Humans... Have you forgotten something?
How was the lift? Nailed it, of course!
Welcome to my forge. I'm Destras, the blacksm...
Hey, wait a second! What's that face for?
Not what you were expecting?
You better not make me mad. I could mould you into a horse trough with this forge, you know!
Alright... Maybe I'm imagining things, but be careful. I've got my eye on you.
My work is my passion, I can't refuse any assignment. Tell me, scrawny, what do you need?
In case you haven't noticed, we Dwarves are busy people, so get to the point, I have things to do.
Yes? What's the matter, soldier?
Don't tell me you're tired of running back and forth.
Enjoy! You can do it! General Brigard has given us captains very clear instructions to hold our position within the city.
But it's sooo boring...
Also, what happened to all the fame and glory after the battle we were going to fight in Zarga?
Are we really going to miss all that?
The best thing about a big punch-up is the huge party afterwards.
Come on, don't waste time telling me your troubles. Go while you can.
Though it may not seem like it, right now, I have dozens of eyes around the city.
If there's a Guardian out there, my rangers will find it.
Although... I wish they still used horses for it.
The fantastic creatures of this world are not really my cup of tea.
Fantastic creatures in general are not my cup of tea...

Oh! Has this library also caught your eye? It's bursting with information about other worlds, beings, races... It's incredible that such a place exists and even more so that we're in it! Arkzel would be amazed by all this information. I have to find out everything I can while we're still in this city.
Yes... yes... We'll talk later. This book of item enchantments is extremely useful. Now, what could I use to practice it on...?
I'm amazed you got out of there alive. You know there were other ways out of that cave, right? But rest assured, your achievements in exploring that room have been recognised.
Who do we have here?
The heroic spider exterminator!
Pfff... It was nothing. It's strange for an ally to attack you, that's why I was surprised.
You had a good look around this city?
It seems like a perfect place to stay, but apparently not even a place like this can escape poverty...
The usual story: poverty, vandalism, order and "so long" to a dignified life.
Anyway, soldier, have fun exploring this world until we get out of here.
I, for one, have done enough... and I have the scars to show for it.
Are you the soldier everyone is talking about lately?
It seems that your adventures are beginning to resonate throughout the city.
What is it like to receive recognition from others?
It's something I'm starting to think I'll never experience...
They think I don't notice, but I'm always left in my sister's shadow.
I'd like to show my worth more than just standing guard.
Or maybe I should accept that they see me as obedient with no aspirations...
Your first achievement was opening the secret chamber in that cave...
Were you afraid?
I mean, that may have been a good place to find the Guardian, but I heard Sinka talking about a horrifying monster.
As terrifying as that story is, I think I would have liked to experience that fear myself.
Oh well... I'll keep waiting for an opportunity.
Oh, it's the tin man! Feel free to look at my maps if you need something, yes?
Have you seen the huge variety of beings and races that coexist in this place?
Do you say that with excitement or fear?
With excitement, of course! Isn't just unbelievable?
Now that I've seen it, it seems pretty believable to me, but I prefer to stay in here, to be honest.
What an adventurous spirit...
What's up? We're rather busy at the moment, to be honest...
Yes, yes, the Human newcomers. Enjoy your stay and everything, or do whatever you want, but don't talk to me.
Good work, soldier! I knew I was right to entrust you with this mission.
Are you alright, soldier? What kind of beings have the power to control those they touch?
Back here again! Everyone's talking about your trip to the western lands. I've never seen anywhere like what the travellers from there say.
When you get a chance, come back and tell me what the Great Pyramid's like inside.
Galath
I never expected Galath to fall in battle.
Still, the situation is the same. His army continues to outperform our own and in great numbers, too. Each second we spend here takes us further away from victory.
The Pyramid
An entire arduous journey for nothing._100_ At least it served to rule out those lands in our search.
Jivan
That Jivan is incredible, and not just because he went around the city putting an end to those beasts as if it were nothing.
From what I can tell, he had the entire city surrounded by a magical shield for several days. Even when he spoke with us, he held enough focus to keep it intact.
It's somewhat daunting to think that someone with that much power exists...
Invasion
None of us expected this. We've lost many of our own in the attack and those who were lucky have been left unconscious.
Those things must be responsible for the attacks on soldiers we've been hearing reports of...
Stay vigilant, soldier, and stay far away from those parasites.
Well, if it isn't the General's lapdog!
Oh, shush! Don't get offended, I wasn't being serious.
There's not really any other choice than obeying the higher-ups.
By the way, since you're always galavanting around this world...
I didn't ever imagine asking you a favour, but if you help me, I'll teach you a trick I think you'll like.
Ha! Spoken like a true soldier of Zarga! Of course!
Listen, there's a mineral called <color=OBJ>garnerock</color>. It's extremely tough but very light and flexible at the same time.
In fact, one of my daggers is made from the very same material.
Exactly! You're a clever one, ain't ya? Garnerock is mainly used to make weapons.
But it's a rare material and not at all easy to find which makes the cost of these weapons sky high.
Some time ago, someone entrusted me with these daggers but, stupidly, I lost one of them.
I wonder if garnerock exists in this world..._100_ It might be a common mineral here or even more abundant than back home.
Either way, if you see someone carrying a weapon with a red blade or something similar, try to find those fragments and being them to me.
You know where to find me. If you have something, I'll be waiting.
Is that real?_100_ Yes! It has to be garnerock!
To be honest, I sent you to find it so you could go and get lost for a bit, but there really is garnerock in this world!
Sendal... I'll get them back to you one day.
Err... Soldier, I'm grateful, really.
Here, as promised. Take these little guys. Sharpen your aim and you'll see how useful they can be.
Thanks again.
I don't think they trust me very much. What's new, eh? Don't trust that shoplifter Sinka.
Well, you know what?_100_ So be it.
Only Sendal treats me like a person...
Eh?_300_ Oh, don't mind me, I was thinking out loud.
And don't spy on me!
I know...
You and I have seen this before.
Those things gave off the same aura we saw in the Spider Lair.
What do you think their goal is, controlling the soldiers like that?
If I were you, I'd be very, very careful to make sure something like that didn't touch me.
I cannot break my promise... I swore I'd keep her safe._100_ Please, hurry.
You don't need to stay here, soldier. I know you're worried about Edil and your own but, from now onwards, I can take care of this.
Go, do what you have to._100_ Preparing for this cure spell is going to take some time.
Hey, is it really true that you and Adamont were trapped and escaped from a pyramid in the desert?
Must've been tough...
Putting up with Adamont, I mean.
There's no captain in all of Zarga grumpier than him. He wouldn't know how to have fun if his life depended on it.
Actually, sorry, I think there is one situation which I've seen him enjoy.
When he has to bash someone's head in.
Basically, Adamont scares me.
What were those things?
I never turn down a battle, but those giant insects gave me the creeps.
Do you think bug rain is normal in this world? I hope not...
By the way, I heard about the mission you're on.
So you're gonna try to save that girl, then? Such a ladies man...
If you want my advice, I don't recommend making her wait too long.
Anyway, go...
Do you know what binoculars are? Well, neither did I before I came here.
The technology these civilisations have is a bit more developed than our own.
Don't worry about that soldier, he'll recover. The insect didn't touch him.
Though, I still don't understand what happened with those Valkyries.
I can't stop thinking about it...
Your second achievement has been to bring back Captain Adamont...
It's quite rare for a private to be able to have a talent for so many different things.
Must be true what they say about the energy in this world, the way it clings to people, if you're capable of holding it.
I can't stop feeling that I'm wasting time just stood here.
Can you believe that they didn't even let me take part in defending the city?
Looks like they just want to keep me out of things.
I sometimes ask myself why they'd even accept me into Zarga's army.
Perhaps to keep me out of the way and make sure that I didn't cause any bother.
That must be it...
Soldier, do you mind if we speak later? This item enchanting book is really drawing me in right now.
That girl..._100_ Edil._100_ Jivan's teaching her some very powerful magic, though it does put me a little on edge.
She doesn't seem the slightest bit interested in the tutoring she's receiving.
I don't like to admit it, but, compared with him, Arkzel and I would look like complete novices.
Arkzel... I wonder where you are now...
General Brigard's being too much of a pessimist, if you ask me.
The Lion of Dadelm turning up here is a good omen.
You know, cut off the serpent's head and its body'll die too
What?_300_ What do you mean it doesn't work like that?
Either way, the mangy cat's still around._100_ He'll be waiting for the slightest chance to pounce on us.
We'll be ready.
Are you alright?
It's such a shame what happened to that girl.
Those blasted things..._100_ They've affected many of our men, too.
I hope the owl can cure them.
AH!
I hate having to wait without being able to do anything.
It's an honour to have you at the best item store._300_ Well, the only item store...
It's the first time something like that's happened in Hafin. Good thing you lot were here to help us!
Got some asgarite we can work with?_100_ Let's have a look...
I only work with <color=OBJ>ragnarite</color> and <color=OBJ>rokirite</color>, so if you don't have enough, let's not waste each other's time.
If I wanted anything to do with all of you, I'd be up there, don't you think?
Why don't you do something more fitting of your place and go chase pichitis?
Is that possible?
speaker: BALOF

text_en: I thought my glasses were fogging up._300_ Wait..._100_ Actually, yes they are.
speaker: BALOF

text_en: Honestly, you took so long to get here that I thought something had happened to you. I did think about going to find you but, as you can imagine, I'd prefer not to set foot in that cave for a while.
speaker: BALOF

text_en: I give you Hafin, the eternal city.
speaker: BALOF

text_en: Now that you're here, I can reward you properly. You didn't think I was only going to give you some of my spare bombs, did you?
speaker: BALOF

text_en: A couple of days ago, I found the perfect gift for you at home.
speaker: BALOF

text_en: Although I lost it again shortly after...
speaker: BALOF

text_en: I know! Why don't you wander around the city while I figure out where I left it?_100_ I'm running home. Don't go far until I find it!
speaker: BALOF

text_en: I'll see you at my place in a little while.
speaker: BALOF

text_en: Come on, Edil, it doesn't normally take you so long to get to this part.
speaker: JIVAN

text_en: I'm doing what I can!
speaker: EDIL

text_en: No, you're not concentrating. Do you think I don't realise that your head is in the clouds?
speaker: JIVAN

text_en: Bah, it's useless.
speaker: EDIL

text_en: Maybe if, instead of just teaching me magic, you'd actually let me use it some time...
speaker: EDIL

text_en: We've already talked about this. I teach you these powers so that you can defend yourself, not for you to use them unnecessarily.
speaker: JIVAN

text_en: But...
speaker: EDIL

text_en:
No "buts", Edil. You are a smart girl; you just need to focus on what you're doing.
Rest for a while and we'll try again later.
speaker: JIVAN

text_en: Okaaay.
speaker: EDIL

text_en: Welcome, soldier. This city will take us in.
Soldier!_100_ Come, I need to discuss a matter in private.
speaker: BRIGARD

text_en: Huff... Huff... There you are.
If you ate more, you'd be less tired.
If you didn't eat all the supplies, maybe I would.
Come on, let's not dwell on things.
Yes..._100_ this..._100_ Soldier, Brigard sent us to find you.
What have you done now?
It's none of our business, Gruper. I think the less we know, the better...
Well, we've already told you. Brigard is waiting for you at Zarga Marquee.
Gruper, get a move on, this issue is still going to affect us.
Take care, soldier. We're off.
I hope I'm not the first to welcome you to Hafin, soldier.
speaker: JIVAN

text_en: Yes, I know what you must be thinking._100_ "Why is there a city in the afterlife?"_100_ Indeed, all of Terragaya's inhabitants perished at some point, then our souls were "rescued" by the Valkyries.
speaker: JIVAN

text_en: I'm sure you think you must fulfil your mission. That is normal. After all, they are the ones who brought you here.
speaker: JIVAN

text_en: But you know what? We are still the masters of our own destiny. What did they promise you? Glory and unimaginable powers if you place yourself in the service of the Gods? I don't believe in such a fate, I've always viewed their mission as a way of helping us make sense of our existence after death, to give us a purpose of sorts.
speaker: JIVAN

text_en: But, honestly, is that what we are to die for? To become embroiled in more war and suffering?
speaker: JIVAN

text_en: I founded this city to be a point of union between all the species that inhabit the universe who are looking for a peaceful eternal life without conflict.
speaker: JIVAN

text_en: I shan't keep you much longer. The fact that you are still in your armour speaks for itself, but know that, if you change your mind, there is always a home for you in Hafin.
speaker: JIVAN

text_en: Best not keep your general waiting.
Soldier, I know you have not had time to rest, but there is something that worries me and that I would like to ask you.
speaker: BRIGARD

text_en: Captain Adamont has been sent on a mission to the Sibuna Desert, west of the sanctuary where these Valkyries brought us.
speaker: BRIGARD

text_en: It has been quite a while since I heard anything from them. Not even Euder's explorers can find him and several of them have even disappeared.
speaker: BRIGARD

text_en: Under normal circumstances, I would not ask this of a private, but you have shown courage in the past and I cannot leave my post while I coordinate the search for the Guardian.
speaker: BRIGARD

text_en: Head to the desert lands of Sibuna and return with what you have discovered.
speaker: BRIGARD

text_en: Survival is not an option, it's an order.
speaker: BRIGARD

text_en: What do you think of the city?
speaker: BALOF

text_en: You're just in time, I just found it. Turns out we've been using it as a tablecloth for a couple of days...
speaker: BALOF

text_en: It's true what they say, the best hiding place is right under your nose.
speaker: BALOF

text_en: Here you are. All yours!
speaker: BALOF

text_en: With it, you can jump again while jumping! You can't get much better than that.
speaker: BALOF

text_en: By the way... your tent fabric is very thin, so I couldn't (nor did I want to) avoid hearing your conversation with that serious fellow with the sword.
speaker: BALOF

text_en: I must say, to reach the Sibuna Desert you'll need to take a huge detour from here. It's a very long journey that will probably end in death and despair.
speaker: BALOF

text_en: But don't worry, there is a way to drastically shorten the trip so much so that even I could make it there, even though I don't like the desert. The heat there makes me smell like bacon and attracts vultures, you know?
speaker: BALOF

text_en: Speak with Gartua, the engineer. You will find him at Hafin's entrance, up the steps. It's unlikely he'll listen to you, but just tell him who you are and what you did for me and he'll help you. That Dwarf owes me more than one favour and I can use it to help you.
speaker: BALOF

text_en: One moment, please. Almost got it...
speaker: GARTUA

text_en:
There.
I hope this is important; I hate my work being interrupted. Of course, I hate many things...
I will turn a blind eye. What's this about?
speaker: GARTUA

text_en: Balof?_100_ Balof sent you...?
speaker: GARTUA

text_en: Wait..._300_ Don't tell me you're that soldier he's been talking so much about!
speaker: GARTUA

text_en: You're a lot smaller than I was expecting, to be honest...
speaker: GARTUA

text_en: Anyway, I understand he's in your debt. And I'm in his debt. If it weren't for the parts Balof brings us, this cannon would still be a mere blueprint, so I'll tend to your request.
speaker: GARTUA

text_en: Let's see..._100_ The place you're heading to is quite inaccessible at the moment, but if I built a lift at the entrance to the Spider Lair, you could easily climb the hill.
speaker: GARTUA

text_en: Shall we get to work?
speaker: GARTUA

text_en: Kraaath!
speaker: GARTUA

text_en: Leave that. We have some freebies to take care of. We'll continue later.
speaker: GARTUA

text_en: Head over there later. Something like this won't take us long.
speaker: GARTUA

text_en: I knew you'd arrive without issues.
speaker: BRIGARD

text_en: Have you seen this? All of these people have lived here for millennia. Without conflict... without dying...
speaker: BRIGARD

text_en: I'd never have imagined a place like this.
speaker: BRIGARD

text_en: But, as idyllic as it seems, we cannot remain here. Zarga needs us.
speaker: BRIGARD

text_en: Hafin City will host us, for now. I have spoken with their overseer and they have allowed us to set up a makeshift camp while we organise; they have even helped us build it.
speaker: BRIGARD

text_en: I recommend wandering around and getting to know its people and businesses.
speaker: BRIGARD

text_en: You also have the other captains at your disposal. Get to know them if you haven't already. We are going to spend some time here coordinating the search for the so-called Guardian.
speaker: BRIGARD

text_en: We shall speak later.
speaker: BRIGARD

text_en: Would you look at that!
speaker: GARTUA

text_en: Mister soldier has finally decided to grace us with his presence!
speaker: GARTUA

text_en: We're pretty busy Dwarves, 'ya know, but bah... this time I'll turn a blind eye. When I see how my projects turn out, I forget all about it.
speaker: GARTUA

text_en: Kraaath!
speaker: GARTUA

text_en: Leave that, I've already told you the chain's tied down enough.
speaker: GARTUA

text_en: Get your things, we're going back to Hafin.
speaker: GARTUA

text_en: Well? What do you think?
speaker: GARTUA

text_en: It's a bit rough and ready, but you can bet your last gold piece that everything we put together's tougher than a quellick's roots.
speaker: GARTUA

text_en: This should settle our debt with Balof. You'll be able to travel to the <color=LOC>desert </color>, now. I'll let you get on, we've got a cannon to build.
speaker: GARTUA

text_en: Let's go, Krath.
speaker: GARTUA

text_en: I heard that Galath, Dadelm's general, is also here. Is it true?
Galath? That man terrifies me. The few times I've seen him he always gave off this aura of endless hate.
He clearly doesn't hold Zarga in high esteem.
By the looks of things, he's got unfinished business with General Brigard leftover from the Dark War.
It had to be humiliating for him when his own king granted the neighbouring kingdom's general official recognition.
You said it.
That was horrible! I thought we'd be safe here.
Though, it's the first time I've seen you wield your sword... and you lived to tell the tale!
That doesn't make it any less horrible.
Stop your whining. Act like a soldier, at least when Brigard's nearby.
I'd prefer to be under Captain Euder's command. He's much more friendly and always seems to be in a good mood.
Pssst...
speaker: EDIL

text_en: Come to speak with the old man? _300_Good luck he's had a bit of an odd day. He's a bit difficult to deal with when he gets all mystical.
speaker: EDIL

text_en: Listen to me carefully...
speaker: JIVAN

text_en: It is difficult to explain, so be prepared to alert your soldiers when I give the signal. We don't have much time.
speaker: JIVAN

text_en: A few days before your arrival, a substance that I was able to identify as hostile agents fell upon Hafin.
speaker: JIVAN

text_en: To ward them off, I created a barrier around the entire city that has kept us safe. I had hoped they would eventually leave, but something appears to be keeping them here.
speaker: JIVAN

text_en: My power is starting to wane, so it won't be long until they arrive.
speaker: JIVAN

text_en: Be careful. Whatever they are, they weren't brought here by the Valkyries.
speaker: JIVAN

text_en: I can't hold it much longer...
speaker: JIVAN

text_en: Old man...?
speaker: EDIL

text_en: What?!
speaker: EDIL

text_en: AH! MONSTERS!
speaker: SOLDIERS

text_en: SOLDIERS, DEFEND THE CITY!
speaker: BRIGARD

text_en: IRONCLADS, GET IN FORMATION!
speaker: ADAMONT

text_en: ON MY ORDERS!
speaker: EUDER

text_en: HELP!
No...
speaker: JIVAN

text_en: The entire city is in danger... Because of me? I must go and help them.
speaker: JIVAN

text_en: Let's go, Edil!
speaker: JIVAN

text_en: No!_100_ I'll defend our home!_100_ He'll help me!
speaker: EDIL

text_en: Edil, we don't have time! Hafin has never faced anything like this before.
speaker: JIVAN

text_en: You prepared me for anything, including something like this!
speaker: EDIL

text_en: Edil...
speaker: JIVAN

text_en: Soldier, please, do not let anything happen to her. She's the most precious thing I have...
speaker: JIVAN

text_en: I will be back as soon as I can.
speaker: JIVAN

text_en: Is that it?_500_ Was that all of them?
speaker: EDIL

text_en: We've defeated them all! Yes!
speaker: EDIL

text_en: Although it's almost a shame, I was starting to have fun, he, he...
speaker: EDIL

text_en: he...
speaker: EDIL

text_en: Huh...?_200_ What's ha...?
speaker: EDIL

text_en: EDIL!
speaker: JIVAN

text_en: EDIL, I'M HERE! PLEASE, SAY SOMETHING!
speaker: JIVAN

text_en: What's happened? Those things... They must have been able to come into contact with her.
speaker: JIVAN

text_en: I'm so sorry, Edil... I shouldn't have left your side.
speaker: JIVAN

text_en: Edil, I can't lose you...
speaker: JIVAN

text_en: Soldier, I don't hold you responsible. It's all my fault. Despite my years, it appears that I'm still making mistakes...
speaker: JIVAN

text_en: If you want to help both her and your friends, there is something you can do.
speaker: JIVAN

text_en: To the east of Hafin, across the plains, you'll find a small orchard with green flowers at the centre: they're called <color=OBJ>Lilis Radiantis</color>.
speaker: JIVAN

text_en: They..._100_ These are no simple flowers. With them, you'll be able to destroy the agent that's keeping her in this state.
speaker: JIVAN

text_en: Hurry, we don't know how much longer they'll stay like this. And be careful, we're managing to defend the city, but these things will surely be roaming the surrounding area.
speaker: JIVAN

text_en: Thank you, I knew I could count on you for this request.
speaker: JIVAN

text_en: You cannot imagine the value these flowers hold.
speaker: JIVAN

text_en: Their curative properties are beyond imaginable, but preparing the flowers will be a complicated process. I will need need harness every ounce of focus I can.
speaker: JIVAN

text_en: I will try to let you know when everything is ready.
speaker: JIVAN

text_en: Strength, Human... I'm sorry, I believe you usually say “greetings”.
speaker: CROMAMINION

text_en: I have a favour to ask you. I know you have no reason to trust me, but I can assure you that I hold no ill intentions.
speaker: CROMAMINION

text_en: I just need you to come with me and listen to our Commander's request.
speaker: CROMAMINION

text_en: Don't worry, it's not a long journey. We're based in the outskirts of the city. After listening, you can decide whether or not to go but, right now, you're our only hope.
speaker: CROMAMINION

text_en: Commander Beliagar. As I expected, the Human has agreed to listen to us.
speaker: CROMAMINION

text_en: Greetings, hormone.
speaker: CROMAMINION

text_en: Greetings, Human. We've called you here because our friend noticed the great courage you showed in defending the city from the invasion of the dark rain.
speaker: CROMACHIEF

text_en: There is much to tell and little time to act, so I'll try to be brief.
speaker: CROMACHIEF

text_en: Certain motives brought us to this world. We believe that travelling here by our own means violates the rules that govern this place, which is why we keep our distance from the city's affairs. We still don't know how all of this works.
speaker: CROMACHIEF

text_en: Our Floating Module is located at a considerable altitude, just above a dense layer of clouds that seem to stay completely still.
speaker: CROMACHIEF

text_en: When we arrived, we came down in our shuttle to begin our research. I'm afraid I can't tell you its purpose but, unexpectedly, an enemy took advantage of the fact that most of our troops were here on the ground and boarded our module. They seem to be airborne pirates that have taken an interest in our technology.
speaker: CROMACHIEF

text_en: These pirates knew what they were doing. They cut the links that would allow us to get back and took the crew who remained inside as prisoners.
speaker: CROMACHIEF

text_en: I'll be honest with you, defending the city is not what has led us to seek you out, but rather the artifacts you use. Those... orbs.
speaker: CROMACHIEF

text_en: During our time here, a certain trader managed to provide us with an orb that would supposedly help us. This orb can release enormous amounts of energy that would reactivate our transport systems. Unfortunately, the orb was inactive and we're unable to use it.
speaker: CROMACHIEF

text_en: We think you may be able to awaken it, as you seem to be quite familiar with them. Would you mind holding it, please?
speaker: CROMACHIEF

text_en: It's not working...
speaker: CROMACHIEF

text_en: We suspected this would happen. After all, these artifacts are entirely new to us.
speaker: CROMACHIEF

text_en: I'm sorry to overwhelm you, Human, but do you believe you could find a way to activate it? Magic is something that escapes our understanding, but we are aware that there are beings in the city who do possess such knowledge.
speaker: CROMACHIEF

text_en: Unfortunately, we're not exactly adept at dealing with Hafin's inhabitants. Most of them seem to fear us... Do you think you could find someone with magical abilities that could awaken its power?
speaker: CROMACHIEF

text_en: Think about it, Human... You may keep the orb until you return. It's not particularly useful to us in its current state. We'll be here if you make progress.
speaker: CROMACHIEF

text_en: Oh! Sorry, sorry! Have you been stood there long? These writings have me completely absorbed. You can't imagine the magical knowledge these volumes hold. We couldn't even dream of such wisdom back in Zarga.
speaker: SIRFIEL

text_en: And all of it's possible right here, where we stand right now! The amount of energy that flows through Terragaya is immense in comparison.
speaker: SIRFIEL

text_en: Hmm?
speaker: SIRFIEL

text_en: Ah... I see. It's not the books that have brought you here, per se. You need to know if there's a way to restore an object's hidden powers.
speaker: SIRFIEL

text_en: Well, I'm sorry to tell you that those types of spells are simply impossible...
speaker: SIRFIEL

text_en: I'm joking! I was pulling your leg! The look on your face was priceless.
speaker: SIRFIEL

text_en: Luckily for you, it looks like pulling off something like that is Magic 101 in this world. The first book I read already featured several studies on how to perform an “energetic awakening”.
speaker: SIRFIEL

text_en: Right, shall we get started?
speaker: SIRFIEL

text_en: Done! That'll be a thousand gold coins, please.
speaker: SIRFIEL

text_en: It's a joke! I'm joking! Oh, aren't you just a gem?
speaker: SIRFIEL

text_en: As your superior, I should be demanding an explanation as to why you're in possession of an element like that, and no, that's not a joke. But I have been keeping track of your achievements under General Brigard's command. He has nothing but praise for you, did you know that? So, I'll trust you. I can only hope you don't get into trouble while Jivan tries to cure our soldiers.
speaker: SIRFIEL

text_en: It's been a pleasure putting this knowledge into practice. If you need something else in the future, don't hesitate to come back.
speaker: SIRFIEL

text_en: You've done it! I knew you would return with the activated orb!
speaker: CROMACHIEF

text_en: Just as the trader said, it emits a huge amount of electrical energy, far more than our magnetic pulses do. This is more than enough energy to activate the transporter.
speaker: CROMACHIEF

text_en: Do you see that beacon on top of our pod? Jump up there. Once you're there, use the orb on the charger's central gemstone. It's an inactive mineral that you can easily recharge to restore the pod's energy.
speaker: CROMACHIEF

STR_DIALOGS_QS_SCRIBLES_REVEILMAPS_PART1_2_3
Tin man? Yes... yes... it is you... I'd never forget armour like that.
Goodness me! I see you've been all over the place. Let's see now... the Sunken Laboratory... the Fire Temple... Dragon Castle...
But you haven't explored them very well... have you? Here's a suggestion: complete 100% of these maps and I'll reward you with something pretty.
Wow! You've managed to reveal all the areas I tasked you with!
You remind me of me in me youth, but with less hair.
STR_DIALOGS_QS_SCRIBLES_REVEILMAPS_PART2_2_3
Hey, I wanted to ask 'ya something.
Do 'ya think these glasses make me look short-sighted?
Heheh... Well, it's quite the opposite. These glasses let me detect all the random junk I come across when I'm out searching.
You know where I'm going with this...
That aero... whatever it is up there in the clouds hasn't exactly escaped my attention.
There are tales about the Croma that talk about this sorta structure, but this is the first time I've been able to see with my own eyes that they exist.
You don't know what that means for someone like me. Croma technology is known across Terragaya, but it's impossible to use here, as vimana minerals aren't naturally occuring in this world.
Which means that machine comes from a different one.
I'm right, aren't I? Don't worry, I don't plan on telling anyone.
But... I would like to ask a mega favour from a mega friend who really admires you.

Could you bring me a few parts from that flying thingamajig? <color=OBJ>Twenty Vimana Cogs</color> should be enough. You have no idea how interested I am in taking a good look at that sorta technology.
It's so exciting to be able to speak with someone who's been up there. Plus, it's you!
If you do me this teensy little favour, I'll give you a special item that's only for VIP customers like you.
I'll be waiting!
Gods above, I'm gonna have a heart attack!
You've managed to find all the parts!
Incredible, just incredible! I can't wait to analyse them.
Oh... I hope you haven't had trouble with the Croma. I wouldn't want to get on the wrong side of one of them.
What would my reputation be if I didn't keep my promises? Here, my latest explosive model.
Use it carefully. It sticks to surfaces and can be detonated from afar. I hope it doesn't get stuck to your hands when you try to throw it.
Huh?
Soldier, don't tell me you're late for training.
I just gave the speech to the others and thought that I could finally get back to reading these huge tomes.
Alright, alright. I'll give you a summary, but you will need to focus. I suppose my reading will have to wait.
As you will have noticed, this world is rich in all kinds of materials, beings and other types of magical elements.
General Brigard has allowed me to put all this knowledge to use so that we may better support our ranks.
So I have permission to treat you all like my guinea pigs. Heh, heh, heh.
Apparently this world hosts little creatures known as <color=OBJ>Bygul</color>.
Generally, they are nothing special, but these writings talk of a bygul variant with a radiant green hue.
These are the ones that interest us. In theory, their healing abilities could be of great use.
So keep an eye out on missions and bring them here if you find any.
I think that, for our first experiment, <color=OBJ>fifteen Radiant Bygul</color> will do.
Is that clear? I thought so.
Return when you've found what we need. Now, I would appreciate some silence. This is a library, after all.
Look how well they light up the library with their eerie glow.
It's simply fantastic that you've managed to find fifteen subjects for our test.
Thanks to your efforts and the essence extracted from these creatures, I've managed to create a formula.
To be quite honest, this is the first time I've tried to potion like this one, so one of two things could happen to you: either it works, or you die.
You think that smile on my face means I'm joking, don't you?
Go on, be brave!
Well, you are indeed a brave one, soldier... I hadn't even explained the formula's benefits to you yet.
It appears I have your trust, at least.
Right, as you still appear to be alive and well, the concoction should increase the curative effects of all <color=OBJ>potions</color> you consume from now on.
Don't tell me that wasn't worth the risk!
Anyway, don't relax just yet, soldier. There's still much for us to do. How about you find another <color=OBJ>fifteen Bygul</color>?
I'm sure you'll be fascinated to know what I can achieve with all those little bugs.
Done! When you've got them, bring them here to me and we'll try out the next formula.
STR_DIALOGS_QS_SIRFIEL_FAIRY_TIER2_PART1_1
STR_DIALOGS_QS_SIRFIEL_FAIRY_TIER2_PART1_2
This place is glowing!
Well, aren't you just an excellent collector.
Well, I imagine you're dying to know what I've managed to cook up with the essence from these insects.
Sorry, but once again you'll need to drink a completely unknown and potentially dangerous concoction Go on...
Aha! Do you feel different?
Your body will now prolong the effects of <color=OBJ>vials</color> on you, meaning you can take advantage of their benefits for longer.
I know the idea excites you, but just you hold on a second, soldier.
Do you think you'd be able to bring me another <color=OBJ>twenty Bygul</color>?
Don't look at me like that. This benefits you more than it does me, after all.
You know where to find me. I'll be waiting patiently.
STR_DIALOGS_QS_SIRFIEL_FAIRY_TIER3_PART1_1
STR_DIALOGS_QS_SIRFIEL_FAIRY_TIER3_PART1_2
They're so cute that they're starting to distract me.
It looks like you've collected the amount I need.
Alright, time for the last formula! Be good and drink this. Do try not to smell it.
You can't imagine how many bygul I've had to crush to make this potion.
I'm joking, soldier. The process is painless. Relax, it'll go down easier...
So, according to the instructions, if you haven't fainted, that means it worked.
From now on, you'll notice an even bigger increase in the effects of the <color=OBJ>potions</color> you consume.
To be honest, I'm delighted to have had an excuse to try out all these formulas. You've been an excellent guinea pig.
Now that we've tested the benefits of bygul essence on you, it's time to apply them to the rest of our army.
Thank you for your contribution to magic.

text_en: Right, we're inside now.
speaker: FISHCHIEF

text_en: It seems to be a kind of laboratory...
speaker: FISHCHIEF

text_en: What is Baydral up to?
speaker: FISHCHIEF

text_en: Chief! We should hurry!
speaker: FISHMINION

text_en: Yes... Human, this is for you.
speaker: FISHCHIEF

text_en: It'll allow you to move around underwater without drowning. Don't bad, right?
speaker: FISHCHIEF

text_en: You're practically Fise now.
speaker: FISHCHIEF

text_en: Chief, I have a question.
speaker: FISHMINION

text_en: Yes, Baiyu?
speaker: FISHCHIEF

text_en: Why have we made them take us all the way here if we haven't come across any underwater areas?
speaker: FISHMINION

text_en: Baiyu... Please...
speaker: FISHCHIEF

text_en: No, seriously. What need was there for them to carry us? We can walk, too.
speaker: FISHMINION

text_en: Baiyu, there's a braj behind you!
speaker: FISHCHIEF

text_en: Hey, soldier! Up here!
speaker: MELIAN

text_en: Don't look at me like that... It's embarrassing enough to have come further than you and then end up trapped here.
speaker: MELIAN

text_en: I wanted to solve this on my own...
speaker: MELIAN

text_en: But hey, now that you're here, I'm glad to see a friendly face.
speaker: MELIAN

text_en: I've been wandering around this passage for a while now, so I think we can work together to clear a path for us.
speaker: MELIAN

text_en: And you can see the <color=OBJ>wind orb</color> in action on the way. Let's go!
speaker: MELIAN

text_en: I told you it'd be useful. Onwards, we can carry on now.
I'll try to find you later.
Good luck!
What?!
speaker: MELIAN

text_en: We've ended up in the same trap!
speaker: MELIAN

text_en: It's my fault. I should have found the way out of these ducts a while back.
speaker: MELIAN

text_en: Don't worry, I'll fix this.
speaker: MELIAN

text_en: Got it!
Unfortunately, it looks like I still can't reach your position.
It's clear we'll need to continue on separate paths for a little while longer.
Good luck, soldier!
That floodgate doesn't have a card reader... Will we be able to open it?
Baiyu, let the important people speak.
(Why don't you just talk to yourself?)
I was referring to the soldierman here.
What do you think? It looks like that capsule contains something with several connections. Perhaps if we break it, it'll cause a system failure in the door.
Break things... Seriously, chief?
Go on, try it.
Oh, bladderwrack! It didn't work...
Wait, chief. You look different. And those hydrobubbles have appeared.
I was just about to mention that, of course.
Mister soldierman, you feel different, right? Try using that energy on the hydrobubbles. We'll find another way.
Come on Baiyu, don't linger.
Go on, deal with that capsule. Let's see what happens.
Don't mind the chief. We left our home halfway through his training.
Now! That appears to be its energy source. Yank it out of there!
HA! I knew I'd find the toy first.
Sorry, sister, I don't plan on sharing it with you.
Damn it!
I knew you wouldn't tell me! Selfish as usual!
Always ruining my fun. I might just be tired of having a sister. You'll be next.
How dare you!
If you hadn't been so meddling...
I wasn't going to let you go alone...
This place doesn't feel right...
Chief, it appears to be their main laboratory. Surely if we look at their research...
Tone down the chitchat, Baiyu. I say we should take a peak at Baydral's studies.
Chief, there are all sorts of things here, and all of it is beyond insanity.
Focus on what matters: the curse of the braj.
But our problem is nothing compared to his other plans.
Baiyu, what are you talking about?
Have you seen those murals? It look like he's trying to hybridise saltwater and freshwater Fise.
I must say, it does look a bit sinister...
Is that Hafin Dam?
What was that?
Is it Baydral? We've been to every part of his laboratory and he hasn't turned up anywhere.
Mister soldierman... Would you mind taking a look?
Shouldn't we go with him?
I think figuring out what's going on here is more important right now.
Don't take your eye off those manuscripts.
So, please, if it's Baydral, tell us.
I still don't know what he plans to do with the dam, but it doesn't look good. Can you check what that noise was while we try to figure this out?
There's several lifetime's worth of work here. Baydral certainly hasn't beaten about the kelp. I hope he doesn't mind if we make a bit of a mess of it.
Meddlesome cretins!
You should stay in that beloved city of yours... While you still can...
Did you think we Fise would spend the rest of our existence in a world like this?
You're just an naive as I was in the past, but you'd best start forgetting about your feeble structures. Now it'll be you who will have to adapt to my world.
Because soon there will be nothing but ruins under the raging storm of my revenge!
Muahahahaha...
Hello again, soldier.
I was trying to help our friends find what they were looking for.
But I don't understand a word of these writing, to tell you the truth...
Of course, they're in Fise.
It was Baydral, right?
He was there...
Really? Will he help us? Where is here?
Baiyu, I don't think he's there anymore.
Really?
Seriously?
I've ended up behind again. I knew I was taking too long.
Well, I can't complain. It's been exciting, to be honest.
What will you do now without that scientist of yours?
Chief?
We have no other choice, Baiyu. We'll stay here to find the cure for the braj and we'll take it to the Land of the Waterfalls.
I suppose this is “goodbye”, then. Without Baydral, Hafin City is saved. The earthquakes have stopped and the dam will no longer burst.
Will you be alright here?

We spent so long thinking we were cursed. Once we arrived here, we discovered that Baydral, a legend in our world, had become twisted over the years, a recluse in this place, and that his “magic” was, in reality, science that turned us into horrible monsters.
It's not what we expected, but we've learnt a lot.
We'll stay here for a while and then Baiyu will take all these discoveries to our home.
Of course I will...
Thank you for everything. You Humans aren't so bad.
Thank you both.
Well, thank you all, I'm feeling more capable by the minute. Take care.
Hey soldier, how about a race to Hafin? We've got good news to deliver!
I'm sorry, it's not safe to enter Hafin's sewers due to the large number of monsters we've recently discovered there. Please be patient while we investigate.
Mixing species, turning them into monsters, flooding the world... Baydral wasn't what we had hoped. It's a good thing you've put an end to all his schemes.
It looks like Baydral wanted to use that orb's power to burst the dam. I can't imagine what drove him to want to do such a thing.
Do not worry about them. The spell is foolproof, without a doubt. Though I will not deny that it has left exhausted.
Tremors
Try not to get too involved. If you see danger, turn away and we shall think of something.
You have already done so much for us.
Parasites
I've never seen creatures like that before, nor have I seen the Valkyries so worried.
I have a bad feeling about all this...
Cannon
Has the cannon at the city gate caught your attention?
Apparently, some time ago, word got around that, if we refused to find the Guardian, he would turn up here and destroy the city in revenge.

I don't really know where that rumour came from, but many took it as truth and began constructing the “Godkiller”, as they call them. I can't say I approve, but neither will I deny people their desire to protect this city, whatever motives they may have.
Thank you for everything, soldier. How was Jivan able to free us from these things using just flowers?
I hate to admit it, but perhaps I should focus more on his lessons.
Soldier, I... I'm sorry I attacked you earlier. The fact that I wasn't in control of my actions is no excuse. I do not deserve to be your general.
Sangrigor
I hadn't foreseen the intentions of the Valkyrie that approached us. All of sudden, she launched those things at us and, before we could even realise, we were no longer in control of our own actions.
Parasites
You've realised it too, right?
The threat that attacked the city and which pursues us outside these walls is not normal, nor is it from this world.
Even the Valkyries don't know how they arrived either or what they seek.
I wonder if Jivan knows more about them.
Do you think those Croma people would let me go up to their flying garbageheap if I ask?
Earthquake? What earthquake?
How is this possible?
First it rained down horrible insects and now we're the victims of these earthquakes.
I'm starting to think that this city isn't as tranquil as they had us believe.
Although, to tell you the truth, I'm glad.
It's boring waiting around with nothing going on. At least this way there's some excitement.
I'd help you, but you know... I didn't end up in a particularly good way after our nearly-twenty-metre fall...
Good luck with that.
Fascinating...
The Croma you've met base all of their technology on vimana crystals.
The electromagnetism they emit is in perfect harmony with their own bodies, allowing them to create all kinds of contraptions and gadgets that we could barely even imagine.
They seem to be a highly advanced civilisation. I think I understand why they're not seen so much in Hafin. This city isn't bad, but its advances aren't so different to our own.
What about those earthquakes?
Let me guess... They've lumped you with a mission to investigate them, right?
Well, if you think it'll do something...
I hope you've asked for a big reward in exchange.
Go on and get that key. We'll meet up here later.
If you're looking for General Brigard, he's not here. He's gone out on a mission.
He picked a group of soldiers and left to investigate something after receiving some mysterious information.
He left me behind because I have to stay with the bounty board, of course, but... why didn't he take you, Makerel?
Because I'm too good to risk and he's left me in charge of the care and defence of our strategic location.
You like to think that, don't you?
What will we do if we lose our general?
Calm down, Makerel, one of the captains will take over his role, don't panic.
Though, you don't have any reason to worry. He's safe thanks to wise old Jivan and the help of our friend, right?
It's true, at this rate you could be Zarga's next general if something happened.
Please, do whatever it is you need to do with that key, do but it quickly.
First General Brigard was attacked by those insects.
And now this...
It seems that misfortune never visits alone.
It's a good thing you and Captain Euder found each other while investigating the same area.
That Valkyrie was lucky. If she came across me...
Best not go near any of us again.
They say that both Jivan and Baydral were some of the first beings brought to Terragaya. I'm not surprised, they seem to have so much power...
I see, so Baydral was behind everything.
That explains a lot.
The distance, the change in attitude...
In another time, he was a good friend and a wise advisor who you could trust.
It's a shame that not everyone is capable of finding peace here. Time always takes its toll in one way or another.
Remember: near the mines on the Tempes Plains. I'll be waiting eagerly, with my stick...
YAH!
YAH! Taste my slightly rusty steel!
How goes it, soldier...?_500_ You were able to put a stop to those earthquakes..._500_ Right...?
My muscles are still stiff..._500_ But with a bit of training..._500_ It'll all will work itself out...
This girl, Edil..._500_ She's very keen..._500_ She's helping with my recovery..._500_ And learning to fence...
She'll make a good soldier...
Were the pig bombs useful? No need to carry too many but make sure you don't run out; you never know when you're gonna need 'em.
Looks like I had no need to worry. This cannon, even while unfinished, can take anything.
So, looks like we're gonna be good buddies after all. What can I hammer for you?
So even under this city you can find dangers...
Once again the hero saves the day.
Are you alright? You're paler than usual.
If I didn't know you better, I'd say something was seriously wrong.
Take it easy, or you'll end up as serious as Brigard.
I read something curious about this city's construction.
Did you know who the founders were? Jivan, a person known as Lady Sibunier and no less than Baydral himself.
From what I can tell, these three were the highest authority in Hafin and took in anyone who decided to stay under their protection.
Unfortunately, Lady Sibunier disappeared and Baydral, with time, became unhinged. He lost the respect of much of Hafin's inhabitants, turning miserable and sullen.
Maybe living that long isn't as great as it seems. What would have to go through his head for him to spend the rest of his days cooking up who knows what sort of plans...
So, have you won your key to the city yet?
Looks like that lad Melian is learning from you. Lately he hasn't stopped bouncing around the city.
I was less nervous when we were being rocked by earthquakes.
At least try to make sure he doesn't break anything. That lad seems a bit fragile for soldier, but I 'spose he shows his brave side when he has to.
We make a good team! My sister has to involve me more from now on.
General Brigard won't stop training, even though they've asked him to get some rest.
I spose' he can't help it. If he didn't have urge to outdo himself, he wouldn't be Zarga's general.
By the way, were you the one who made the earthquakes stop?
Who else?
Yeah... I don't know why I asked that.
Seems like word's gotten around that you and the other guy saved the city.
I'm proud of you!
To be honest, I knew Sirfiel's brother was tough enough for this. All he had to do was try.
So, you've worked together with those fish people? I'd never have imagined that beings like that existed, let alone that they'd cooperate with Zarga.
Although I suppose I shouldn't be so surprised. It seems that anything's possible in this city.
My people will be forever in your debt. My sincerest thanks for helping us.
Our goal now is to find the origin of those parasites. We've come all the way from our own planet in search of it.
We'll find it, whatever the cost.
Cursed pest.
Did you think I'd just sit by while you slipped behind my back?
Ugh...
Do I look like a Valkyrie to you? A fluttering fool bound to inaction?
No... more like a giant rodent...
How dare you?!
Another bloodsucker...
Alright then, I'll make this quick.
Step away from them, beast!
You know... You're starting to become very annoying.
Whatever you say, but touch them and it'll be the last thing you do.
Big words for someone so insignificant.
Don't underestimate the power of insignificance, monster.
What...?
You- You heard me!
Oh, how I despise you mortals, always punching above your own weight.
I don't have time for your nonsense.
Good, looks like he's gone.
I don't think the two of us would have been able to take that thing on.
Melian!
Melian!
Melian, can you hear me?!
I knew you'd picked up the other volcanic pendant. Melian, how could you? Why did you have to get involved in this by yourself? You don't need to prove anything!
Heh... Look at me... Relying on you again, as always. You must be fed up of it. You should just leave me here, I'll be less of a burden on you and the rest.
Don't ever say that again! You know that you're all I have left since mum and dad died. I don't want... I don't want the same thing to happen with you. You hear me?!
I miss them too... Is that why they never ask me to join in? So that you can take care of me?
No, idiot... It's because I only feel protected when you're around, because I know that no one would worry about me like you would.
I didn't know... I suppose it's painful to talk about it. Looks like all we have is each other, right?
Don't ever do this to me again... From now on, we'll take care of each other, just as mum and dad want. Deal?
You and me against the world. Doesn't sound too bad... Deal.
We should head back. If we don't take care of these wounds soon, they could get serious.
You're coming too, soldier.
Sirfiel, wait.
Friend... You must stop him.
Are you crazy?
You want to go after that monster?
Sirfiel, it's important. Something terrible will happen if nobody stops him.

I don't know what you've got yourself into, but we can't send reinforcements here, I don't have enough materials for more amulets either. You best be extra cautious if you plan to face that monster and come back in one piece.
Come closer, friend, I have to tell you something...
I can't use this anymore. I'd like you to keep it and continue what we've started. You know what's at stake...
You haven't let go of that orb since you found it. Will that be enough to save him?
Don't worry, sister. He knows how to take care of himself.
Alright...
We're leaving. Come back soon or I'll have to worry Brigard.
Look at it. The gift of the Gods, Yggdrasil.
Some worship it, others fear it.
But wherever it is, this tree has the ability to change the fate of the world.
Even in Terragaya, where it has stayed hidden for millennia.
What are you doing here, mortal?
You're in such a rush to die that you can't wait until I'm done with Yggdrasil?
Alright. If that's what you want, you'll get one chance to stop me.
After this, I'll bite its roots and everything will end.
Show me the determination that brought you here! Defend yourself!
Ugh...
I hope you know the consequences of what you've avoided here...
If you're that desperate to find the Guardian, I'll tell you where he is.
Head east until you reach a large platform. On it, place this cube. It's a key. It'll take you to the place you're looking for.
Now it's on you to fix this.
What an unfortunate sight... I don't think you're capable of finishing off those roots right now.
I suppose those mortals weren't following me for the sake of it....
What will happen with the plague now if you don't destroy the tree? And why have you given that Human the key to Beigon?
You know very well what will happen. You yourself have seen how unstoppable it is. At this rate, it'll wipe everything out, and it'll be just a matter of time before it reaches the Sea of Oberon.
They're that afraid of it?

You've instilled those little mortals with so much confidence, at least get them to the end. The plague's origin lies there. That's why I took the key, so no one could open the Guardian's chamber. But I'm guessing you knew all that...
Are you sure about this?
My nose never fails me. Now it's up to you to do something.
Huh?
So it's still not over then?
Alright, I wouldn't want to disappoint..
First that monster and now you.
Did it really have to end like this...?
The beast that both you and that other boy describe...
It seems to be a Feral, a creature whose energy rivals that of the Valkyries...
My suspicions proved correct. If that creature has been here, it can't have been for a good reason.
It's important you tell me exactly where you faced him. I must see it with my own eyes.
No... Do not worry, I shall take care of it. If he really has revealed the location of the Guardian to you, you'd best take his word as truth.
Lying doesn't come naturally to those beasts.

I think it'd be the perfect sword for me!
I spose' that, if you bring it to me, I'd have to change my mission from finding it to taking it back, once I've learnt to use it.
What'dya say? Do you accept my quest?
YAH!!

Heheheh. No one stands a chance against us!
How goes it, soldier? Come to tell me about your latest achievements?
Well, I was just thinking about sending you on a new and exciting adventure myself.
Seeing our general train was fantastic! I want to be just as skillful with a sword as he is!

Some soldiers are taking assignments, come take a look, don't be shy! Any monster you defeat will make this place a little safer.
If you defeat one, talk to me. I'm the treasurer.

A reward is offered for defeating Kalli the Pyromaniac. He was last seen in the <color=LOC>Spider Lair</color>.
Seriously? You read this and decide to return to that horrid cave, just like that?
It wasn't that bad... It was well decorated.
Gruper, at the very least they made human sacrifices!
Hmm...
What?
The glass is always half empty for you.
What about your belly? Is that half empty or half full?
I knew you'd be back in one piece. I hope it wasn't too traumatic going back to that lair...
Congratulations, you've embarked on the path of a bloodthirsty warrior.
A reward is offered for putting an end to Belnis Two-Eyes and his misdeeds. Last seen lurking in the <color=LOC>Forest of Fyr</color>.
A Reynis... scary!
You know you say the same thing every time someone comes along and picks up one of those, right?
Don't they scare you?
Of course not, but we're on guard duty here in the tent, so I can't go anywhere without explicit orders from General Brigard.

Hey, friend, know why they call him “two-eyes”? It's very common for the more experienced Reynis to end up losing an eye. That lot are a dangerous bunch, but this is a Reynis that rose up through the ranks with both eyes intact, meaning he's basically a king in a one-eyed world.
You look inspired...
You're back! Was it hard facing someone with two eyes?
Gruper, are you seriously asking him that?
A juicy reward goes to whoever kills the Stygian Harpy and drives her foul pack of vultures away from the <color=LOC>Sibuna Desert</color>.
Harpies are half women half birds, right?
I've been wondering for a good while now why you know so much about the monsters here.
Because I, unlike some, know how to listen. I'm always telling you.
So, do they have a chicken's head and a women's legs?
Mahaha! Their upper half's from a woman and their legs are from a chicken.
What's so funny? If it were up to you, they'd have chicken thighs for a head.
So, which part was chicken then?
Ignore him... Here you are. Have you ever thought about switching jobs?
A reward is offered for defeating the Brothers of the Golden Guard, thereby bringing an end to the slavery at the <color=LOC>Great Pyramid</color>.
Gruper, what do you know about those two?
They say the Brothers of the Golden Guard raid this city from time to time in order to kidnap people and make them their slaves, forcing them to build their pyramids in the desert to the west.
Weren't the Spider Acolytes the ones who ladnapped people to sacrifice?

How do they cope? So stressful...
I wasn't sure if you'd be able to do it. It was two against one, after all. Still, I had my bets on you.
Me too, of course.
A reward is offered to whoever puts an end to the mud golem frightening the cattle. It has been sighted dragging itself across the <color=LOC>Tempes Plains</color>.
A golem made of mud...
What?
Isn't it strange?
What's strange about it? Until a moment ago you didn't know golems existed.
They exist in our world too. Did you know that?
Those were golems? I thought they were robots...
Well, they always have a magical element to them. It seems like beings from this world are made from nature itself, like the stone ones. Is a mud golem a dirty golem?
You spend the entire day thinking about this sort of thing, don't you?
So... was it a dirty golem?
Does it really matter? Give him his reward so that he can carry on dealing with those monsters.
A reward is offered for dealing with Joki the Mad, recently sighted in the clouds above Hafin.
The clouds...
Sound familiar to you? Your head often spends quite a while up there, doesn't it?

Well, our friend here's been up there. Is it really true that there are sky pirates?
They're known as the Pirates of the Broken Wing.
They don't seem very dangerous...
What do you mean?
Imagine I was some outlaw and I called myself “The Broken Leg”. Would that really fill you with fear?
Makerel, you could call yourself whatever you wanted and I doubt you'd fill ever anyone with fear.
Looks like the Pirates of the Broken Wing have taken yet another nasty blow from you.
I still don't think that names very catchy...
A reward is offered for destroying my crea- a very evil monster who traipses uncontrollably around the <color=LOC>Sunken Laboratory</color>. Its name is Project 0.5 (pre-alpha).
Makerel, why don't you go with him this time?
Why don't you go?
Because I'm the treasurer.
I haven't heard that one before...
I'm needed here to give the soldiers who complete tasks their rewards.
Soldiers plural? He's practically the only one who's dealing with the local fauna. I doubt he needs me.
So you think General Brigard needs you more, then?
Yes...? No... I spose' not... But these are my orders and I don't plan on moving from this spot.
What a firm soldier you are, when it interests you...
What did that creature look like? There weren't a lot of details in the assignment.
Argh! Tentacles? Actually, please stop there, I'd rather not know...

A reward is offered for killing the monster known as the Summoner Soul for having put us in grave danger by willingly increasing the number of monsters in the area. It was last seen entering the sealed door in the <color=LOC>Forest of Fyr</color>.
The sealed door of the Forest of Fyr...
This assignment must be an old one. I heard the brother of Captain Sirfiel say that you'd managed to get into that place.
The lad idolises you more than he does General Brigard.
So, you going for the reward? With a name like that, sounds it could be one of the more dangerous ones.
A monster that summons monsters! I don't even want to imagine it.
Although it looks like you only get paid for the main one. Shame.
I don't think he cares. Something tells me that our friend here isn't as greedy as you.
Why do I even say anything?
And once again you're back. I'd be delighted to hear all about your grizzly fight with that Summoner Soul.
I don't... plan on sleeping tonight.
A handsome sum goes to whoever manages to kill the tempestuous Avalerion. This bizarre creature is disrupting the local ecosystem on the <color=LOC>Tempes Plains</color>.
Why would anyone pay to have a vulture killed?

But they're still birds, right?
I'll explain with an example: Did the spiders in that cave seem like simple arachnids to you?
Makerel? You've gone all white.
You just had to remind me of them, didn't you?
Did you manage to defeat that Avalerion? I thought it might've flown off with its reward after feeling threatened.
Luckily for our friend here, that bird was as keen to fight as he was, wasn't it?
Oh... Would you look at that!
Keep your hair on. What's happened?
The board. There's no more assignments!
You mean he's gotten rid of all the monsters?
All the ones that came with a reward attached, indeed. My coffers are empty.
Good news! This world suddenly seems a little safer. Thank you, friend, makes you feel like crying.
Who needs to keep their hair on now? Anyone would say you're having a harder time than he is.
You might be right there!
Well, we're not talking about you, Makerel.
General Brigard said that he had a special prize for the person who could rid us of more monsters, and that's you!
More money?
No idea. Give him the good news and find out, you've earnt it.
So it's true. You've completed the bounty board.
It makes me proud that you've been willing to pay back Hafin's favour to us.
You have settled our debt with this city, so I shall honour my promise.
Soldier of Zarga, as General of the kingdom's army, it is my honour to present you with the Shimmering Blade of Zarga.
I know you'll put it to good use.
THERE ARE NO NEW MISSIONS AVAILABLE.
You're back!
Thank the Gods you're alright... I never would have forgiven myself if something happened to you.
I suppose I should stop being so surprised at your achievements.
Me? It's nothing... Don't worry, Jivan says that I'll recover.
So, you saved this world without anyone even realising what was about to happen?
It's simply incredible that you were able to kill that beast, but something tells me that, if anyone could've, it'd be you.
How are you handling the wind orb? Looks like you've got a better grasp of it than me. That's not exactly unexpected though, you've been using those orbs for quite a while now.
No! You don't need to give it back to me. I think, from now on, I'll look for value in myself, though it would be nice to see its tricks in action.

Here's a thought... Would you dare go back to that temple? I'm sure you saw that ancient amphitheatre. I think if we get their attention enough, some of those monsters will come out and we can practice on them.
I think I can sneak out as long as my sister doesn't get wind of it. Facing her would definitely be a challenge...
What do you say?
When you want to try out your skills with those orbs, let me know. I don't want to miss it. That amphitheatre at the Fire Temple seems like the perfect place.
Really? Say no more! We'll need to head back before my sister finds out.
You're right, perhaps I've gotten excited than I should have. Though, if you change your mind, I'd be delighted to go with you.
Why not?
Another time, then.
I'm speechless. It's a good thing you're one of our own.
I'd be lying if I said I wasn't jealous, but that's just how it is.
I'm looking forward to recovering so that I can put what I've learnt from you into practice.

You...

Report 1

We find ourselves quite far from home, but it seems that we have reached a habitable planet full of interesting life to be discovered. I do hope we haven't been too hasty in our decision. I believe we have found the perfect creature. We call it, the “Blink”.

Blinks are elusive and managing to capture several of them has been quite the feat. Fortunately, all of their insight is reduced to zero when sleeping in packs. The main reason for my choice is their ability to move from location to location from one moment to the next. I have never seen anything so fast in the history of Kortia's games.

We have enough specimens. Tomorrow we will embark on our return trip. I'm simply dying to present the committee with our candidates. It's a shame we cannot take part this year, but it will be most interesting to see what strategies the other modules employ in an attempt to capture them.

I must capture it and discover what drives it.

In any case, we are here for revenge. The being is on the surface. Now is our chance to go down there and face it directly. Should we fail, other worlds will meet the same fate as our own.

Our transporters are ready. Once we reach a suitable altitude, we will launch them at the surface, descend and begin our hunt. We have travelled across the entire galaxy to get here. Day 33.

Being infected by that parasite has changed me, there is no doubt about it.
The feeling of suffocation gives way to defeat and submission. It plays with you, leaving you lucid one moment and in a blind fog the next, manipulating your actions and thoughts. There's a strange sensation of power. It awakens abilities in you that you didn't even think were possible and exploits your potential. Experiencing that has made me go back to thinking about Arkzel again. If that parasite brought out that much power in me... What could it do to someone like him? Was the earthquake just a coincidence? The more I think about it, the closer I get to believing it wasn't.
I hope you're alright, old friend.

If you've found this, my unknown friend, I want you to read my last words. I won't lie to you, they're out of desperation – the very same sensation you'll soon feel if you venture further into the darkness of this cave.

Such a bleak way to go. I've spent most of my second life trying to find a way to break into the mythical Fire Temple. Bewildered by these markings, I was far from noticing that countless creatures had closed in behind me and blocked my way out.

Once I realised my grave mistake, I ran faster and faster, and further and further inside. I've survived long enough to figure out that <color=CHA>these creatures are vulnerable when exposed to light</color>. However, when in the shadows, the darkness they've become so accustomed to over the years fuels their violent frenzy, rendering them an unstoppable threat.

This is my last torch. The blanket of light that protects me slowly fades while I watch the eyes around me, peering in eagerly, glowing more and more intensely, waiting for my flame's final sigh.

-Jonein.V-

A thousand titans were struck down before Beigon had selected new protectors to test potential Einherjars. I do wonder how many dragons will have to perish before the Guardian relieves them of this macabre fate.

I understand that his motives are pure, but I only see cruelty in using the lives of these noble creature as a final test.
I am aware that the protector creature's purpose is to repel travellers, but it is quite clear that anyone who comes this far is unlikely to turn back in a hurry.
Tomorrow I shall set out on a long journey in search of creatures more deserving of serving in this manner. Such is my pact with Beigon. They shall be strong and terrifying, as is his wish, but also contemptible enough that their lives will not be worth missing.
